material_decisions.answer: Export every note present in the saved-note store at command start, including notes with empty content.
material_decisions.why_material: Selecting all notes establishes the export boundary and prevents implementations from choosing different subsets.

material_decisions.answer: Emit UTF-8 JSON Lines to standard output, with exactly one compact JSON object per note and a single LF after each object; do not pretty-print or add headings, summaries, or other output.
material_decisions.why_material: This makes “compact” an objective output-shape requirement.

material_decisions.answer: Each exported object contains exactly two fields: "id" and "content". Include no timestamps, tags, storage paths, derived values, or other metadata.
material_decisions.why_material: Exact field inclusion is part of the public output contract.

material_decisions.answer: Order exported notes by ascending Unicode code-point order of their "id" values.
material_decisions.why_material: A deterministic order makes identical saved state produce objectively comparable output.

material_decisions.answer: The decoded JSON string value of each exported "content" field must equal the stored content exactly, including empty content, spaces, tabs, line breaks, Unicode characters, and leading or trailing whitespace. JSON-required escaping is allowed only when decoding restores the exact stored string.
material_decisions.why_material: This operationalizes content preservation without confusing serialization escapes with content changes.

material_decisions.answer: Export is read-only: it must not create, update, delete, reorder, normalize, rewrite, or persist any change to saved notes or their metadata.
material_decisions.why_material: This defines the central data-safety boundary.

material_decisions.answer: If the saved-note store cannot be read completely, emit no export records, write a diagnostic to standard error, return a nonzero exit status, and leave the store unchanged.
material_decisions.why_material: Partial output and failure behavior affect whether consumers can trust an export as complete.

material_decisions.answer: Adding export must not change the stored data, standard output, standard error, or exit status of existing create, read, update, delete, list, and persistence workflows for the same inputs and initial state.
material_decisions.why_material: The feature is additive and must not alter established note behavior outside export.

owner_rules: Treat each material decision as independently required and preserve it without broadening or weakening its modality, scope, exceptions, failure result, or verification meaning.
Require acceptance coverage for multiline content, empty content, leading and trailing spaces, tabs, non-ASCII Unicode, JSON-special characters, and notes with metadata that must not be exported.
Require a before-and-after stored-state comparison proving that both successful and failed exports leave all note content and metadata unchanged.

Require regression verification for representative successful and failing create, read, update, delete, list, and persistence workflows, comparing stored state, standard output, standard error, and exit status.

question.prompt: What should the export command produce? This choice changes how users invoke it and how the exported notes can be consumed.

options.label: JSON to stdout
options.description: Emit compact machine-readable JSON to standard output, allowing redirection to a file without modifying saved notes.

options.label: JSON file
options.description: Require a destination path and write compact machine-readable JSON directly to that file.

options.label: Plain text
options.description: Emit a concise human-readable representation that is easier to inspect but less reliable for reprocessing.

JSON document shape and which note fields/metadata must be included
Which saved notes are exported: all notes or an explicitly selected subset

question.prompt: Should one invocation export every saved note or only notes explicitly selected by the user? This determines whether selection arguments and partial-export behavior are required.

options.label: All notes
options.description: Export every saved note with the smallest command surface and no selection syntax.

options.label: Selected notes
options.description: Require one or more note identifiers so users can export a precise subset.

options.label: Both modes
options.description: Export all notes by default while optionally accepting identifiers for a subset, increasing interface and testing scope.

JSON document shape and which note fields or metadata must be included
Meaning of “compact”: minified JSON output, short command syntax, or both

question.prompt: What should each exported JSON entry contain? This changes whether exports preserve only note content or also retain identity and available metadata.

options.label: Full note records
options.description: Export an array of objects containing each note’s exact content plus its identifier and all existing metadata, preserving the most information.

options.label: ID and content
options.description: Export an array of objects containing only each note’s identifier and exact content, yielding a smaller stable schema but omitting metadata.

options.label: Content only
options.description: Export an array of exact note-content values, producing the smallest output but losing identifiers and metadata.

Meaning of “compact”: minified JSON output, short command syntax, or both

question.prompt: What must be compact? This determines whether compactness applies to the CLI surface, the emitted JSON, or both.

options.label: Both
options.description: Use a short invocation and emit minified JSON with no insignificant whitespace.

options.label: Minified JSON
options.description: Require compact serialized output, while allowing a conventional descriptive command name.

options.label: Short command
options.description: Require a terse invocation, while allowing human-readable pretty-printed JSON.

question.prompt: What exact command should export all saved notes? This choice determines the public CLI syntax users and tests will rely on.

options.label: notes export
options.description: Use a clear namespaced command that leaves room for other note operations.

options.label: export
options.description: Use the shortest command, with greater risk of ambiguity if the CLI later exports other data.

options.label: notes --export
options.description: Use a flag-style invocation, which is terse but less conventional for a distinct operation.

question.prompt: How should `notes export` behave if it cannot read saved notes or cannot complete writing valid JSON to stdout? This determines whether callers can reliably detect a failed or incomplete export.

options.label: Fail nonzero
options.description: Write diagnostics to stderr, return a nonzero exit status, and never intentionally emit JSON when reading notes fails; a stdout write failure also returns nonzero.

options.label: JSON error
options.description: Emit a JSON error object to stdout and return nonzero, keeping output machine-readable but mixing success and error schemas.

options.label: Best effort
options.description: Export readable notes and report skipped or unwritten data, which may produce incomplete results and requires a partial-success contract.

output.answer: If the saved-note store cannot be read completely, emit no export records to stdout, write a diagnostic to stderr, return a nonzero exit status, and leave the store unchanged. If writing the JSON Lines output to stdout fails or cannot be completed, write a diagnostic to stderr, return a nonzero exit status, and leave the store unchanged.
